learning_outcomes.text: Analyze and characterize the operation of hydraulic and volumetric machines, applying the principles of fluid mechanics, similarity laws, and performance criteria to evaluate their behavior under different operating conditions.

Select and size pumping systems and hydraulic installations, determining the operating point, evaluating phenomena such as cavitation and hydraulic transients, and justifying the choice of equipment and pumping stations in urban, industrial, and environmental applications.

syllabus_topics: The Dimensional Analysis: Utility and Justification
Obtaining Dimensionless Parameters and the Pi Theorem
Common Dimensionless Parameters in Fluid Mechanics
Types of networks: branched and meshed networks
General system of equations for steady state
Some simplifications used in network analysis and design
Fundamental Theorem of Turbomachinery or Euler's Theorem
Theoretical head supplied by a pump
Deviation from theoretical behavior: Definition of Losses
Application of similarity laws in hydraulic machines
Introduction to cavitation in hydraulic machines
Physical description of elastic hydraulic transient
Wave speed 'a' of the pressure pulse
Resolution using the method of characteristics
Resolution using the graphical method of SCHNYDER-BERGENRON
teaching_methods: Lectures: Participatory master class, conferences, company visits, attendance at fairs.
Participatory class: Individual or group. Case resolution, role-playing, technique application exercises, oral and written presentations, debates.
Laboratory: Activities carried out in spaces with specialized equipment. Research sessions on classroom didactics.
Integrated project: Realization of a project to solve a problem or address a task through planning, design, and execution of a series of activities.

Tutoring: Personalized and small group attention. Instruction aimed at reviewing, redirecting class materials, learning, and carrying out assignments. Specific student consultations. Scheduled tutorials.
assessment_rules: The course is passed if the final grade is 5 points or higher, and no written test grade is below 4 points. In the first call, unapproved parts can be recovered. If written tests do not reach 4 points, the course is failed. In the second call, project grades are maintained.
